ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-transistor VT amplifier circuit. On the left side, u_i is input through a coupling capacitor to the base node, and this node is also connected to bias resistors RB1 and RB2. Above the collector, RC is connected to +Vcc, and the output u_o is marked on the right side. The resistor R_f is located on the upper right side of the circuit; one end of it is connected to the output/collector-related node, and the other end is connected back to the base input node. Reasoning: R_f samples from the output end and feeds back to the input end, so the output sampling method is voltage sampling; the feedback signal is merged into the base input node in the form of current, and is superimposed in parallel with the input signal at the same node, so the input mixing method is parallel (current parallel) feedback. This stage is a common-emitter amplifier circuit, and the output is inverted 180° relative to the input. The signal returned through R_f weakens the effect of the original input, so it is negative feedback. In summary, what R_f introduces is parallel voltage negative feedback.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the figure, what type of feedback is introduced by resistor \(R_f\)?

method.method_draft: Inspect the figure first: locate R_f and trace its two terminals. One terminal is tied to the collector/output node associated with u_o, while the other returns to the base/input summing node where u_i enters. Classify the output connection as voltage sampling because R_f senses the output node voltage. Classify the input connection as parallel/shunt feedback because the feedback current is injected into the same base input node in parallel with the input signal path. Since the transistor stage is common-emitter and gives 180° phase inversion, the returned signal opposes the input signal. Therefore the feedback introduced by R_f is parallel voltage negative feedback.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: R_f forms a path from the output/collector node back to the base node where the input is applied. For a midband feedback test, replace V_CC by AC ground and regard the coupling and emitter-bypass capacitors as shorts. Apply a hypothetical positive increase of input base voltage; in the common-emitter transistor this causes the collector/output voltage to move in the opposite direction. That output change is coupled through R_f as a feedback current into the base node in a sense that reduces the original input effect, so the feedback is negative. Because the feedback signal is derived from the output node voltage and is mixed as a current at the input node in parallel with the source, name it parallel voltage negative feedback.
